meta.name: IntelliRelease Deployment Strategy Rules
meta.purpose: Maps every SAP Commerce artifact type the Context Engine's knowledge base (sap_context.json) can classify to a deterministic deployment strategy recommendation (ROLLING or MIGRATE), a priority used to resolve conflicts across multiple changed files, and the reasoning/recommended actions a Release Manager sees on the dashboard. Adding a new artifact type here — with no Java change — is enough to teach the Deployment Strategy Engine about it; see docs/deployment-strategy-advisor.md.

defaultReason: No deployment rule is configured for this artifact type yet. Defaulting to rolling deployment; add an entry to deployment_strategy_rules.json to give it an explicit recommendation.

rules.reason: items.xml modifies the SAP Commerce type system — new or changed ItemTypes, attributes or relations require a database schema migration and generated model/DTO regeneration.
A Patch defines a versioned, ordered data migration. It must run as part of a system update, not while old and new application nodes are serving requests side by side.
Patch resource data feeds a versioned data migration and must be applied consistently during a system update.
The Cloud Deployment Descriptor changes aspect topology. Nodes on different manifests are not guaranteed compatible, so the whole environment must move together rather than roll node by node.
Activating or deactivating an extension changes what code and beans exist on a node. Old and new nodes running different extension sets are not a safe rolling pair.
A DTO/bean definition affects the facade layer's data shape, not the database schema. Existing and new nodes can coexist.
Spring bean wiring is a service-layer configuration change, not a schema change.
OCC web/field-set wiring changes the API surface, not the database. Coordinate with the frontend release, but no schema migration is required.
Controllers are business/orchestration logic only — no database schema changes, no type system changes.
A request filter changes request-handling logic in the API layer, not persisted data or schema.
A validator enforces input rules in application code — no database schema changes, no Type System changes.
Business logic only. No database schema changes, no Type System changes — old and new nodes can coexist.
Service-layer business logic. No database schema or type system impact.
A DAO changes how existing data is queried, not the schema it is queried against.
Populators map already-persisted data onto DTOs — application logic only.
Converters transform data in memory — application logic only, no schema impact.
A persistence interceptor runs application-level logic around save/load — it does not itself change the schema.
A pluggable strategy implementation is business logic only.
A method/persistence hook runs application logic around an existing operation — no schema change.
Event publication/handling is application logic — no schema impact.
A business process definition changes orchestration flow, not the database schema. Verify in-flight process instances remain compatible.
A business process action is application logic executed by the process engine — no schema change.
A CronJob/JobPerformable implementation is application logic. Verify its trigger configuration is still correct after rollout.
A key generator implementation is application logic — no schema impact.
Solr search configuration does not change the SAP Commerce database schema. A full reindex is required for the new configuration to take effect.
A Solr field value provider is application logic that runs during indexing — no database schema impact, but affected stores need a reindex.
A CMS component type definition changes application-level configuration, not the underlying database schema.
CMS content ImpEx changes data, not schema. Synchronise the affected content catalog after deployment.
General ImpEx changes data on the target environment — no schema change.
Security ImpEx (user groups, access rights, roles) changes authorization data, not the schema — review access changes carefully before rollout.
Store/site ImpEx changes configuration data, not schema.
Product catalog ImpEx changes data, not schema. Synchronise the affected catalog after deployment.
CronJob/trigger/retention ImpEx changes scheduling data — no schema change. Verify the schedule before enabling.
Integration setup ImpEx changes configuration data for external connections — no database schema change, coordinate with the integration partner if credentials or endpoints move.
An Integration Object / inbound channel / outbound destination is configuration and mapping logic — no SAP Commerce schema change. Coordinate with middleware/ERP.
Hot folder / batch import configuration is application-level configuration, not a schema change.
A System Setup / data import service class is application logic. If it triggers a Patch, that Patch is independently flagged for migrate deployment.
Backoffice configuration is admin-tool configuration — no SAP Commerce schema change.
A Backoffice widget/action/editor/renderer is admin-tool UI code — no schema change.
Backoffice security/wiring is admin-tool configuration — no schema change.
SmartEdit configuration is CMS-authoring tool configuration — no schema change.
An email template is presentation content — no schema or business-logic impact.
A Velocity template is presentation content — no schema impact.
Extension properties are environment configuration — no schema change. Affected aspects may need a restart to pick up the new value.
Environment/persona/aspect properties are configuration — no schema change. Affected aspects may need a restart to pick up the new value.
Local development properties are configuration only — no schema change.
An extension dependency declaration changes the build graph, not the running schema. Rebuild before rolling out.
The project descriptor is build/module configuration — no schema change.
Build configuration affects how the artifact is assembled, not the running schema.
A CI pipeline definition affects the build/release process, not the running application's schema.
A backend localisation bundle is presentation content — no schema impact.
A test file has no runtime deployment impact.
Frontend OCC endpoint/site-context configuration is a storefront-side change — no SAP Commerce schema impact.
Frontend feature registry/CMS mapping is a storefront-side change — no backend schema impact.
A Spartacus/Angular feature module is storefront code — no backend schema impact.
A frontend adapter is storefront code — no backend schema impact.
A frontend connector is storefront code — no backend schema impact.
A frontend service is storefront code — no backend schema impact.
A frontend component is storefront presentation code — no backend schema impact.
A frontend component template is storefront presentation markup — no backend schema impact.
A frontend pipe is storefront presentation logic — no backend schema impact.
CSS/styling changes are purely presentational — no backend or schema impact.
A frontend model/interface is storefront-side typing — no backend schema impact.
A route guard changes storefront navigation logic — no backend schema impact.
An HTTP interceptor changes storefront request/response handling — no backend schema impact.
The frontend root module changes storefront bootstrap/wiring — no backend schema impact.
Frontend translations are presentation content — no backend schema impact.
The frontend dependency manifest changes the storefront build, not the running SAP Commerce schema. Rebuild the storefront before rollout.
Frontend environment configuration affects the storefront build target — no backend schema impact.
Frontend build configuration affects how the storefront is assembled — no backend schema impact.
